title: Cross-Region Key Event Reconciler and Tamper-Evident Audit Export
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Build a service to reconcile KMS and HSM key lifecycle events across regions and produce tamper-evident, per-tenant audit export bundles that map key events to data residency and retention policies. The reconciler will ingest KMS audit logs, HSM-signed change records, and internal rotation events; de-duplicate and order them deterministically; anchor exports with a Merkle root and HSM timestamp signatures; and surface a signed artifact for regulatory reporting and customer evidence requests.
background: Current audit exports are fragmented: KMS logs live in cloud audit sinks, HSM change records are emitted by vendor SDKs, and rotation metadata is scattered in the rotation pipeline. Compliance customers and SOC teams frequently request a single coherent artifact that proves when and where keys were rotated, who triggered the action, and that the export has not been tampered with. Existing Linear tickets improved logging and rotation telemetry, but we lack a production-grade reconciler that correlates events across boundaries and emits a cryptographically verifiable export tied to residency and retention metadata.
goals: 1) Correlate key lifecycle events from KMS, HSM, and rotation pipeline into an ordered timeline per-tenant and per-key-family. 2) Produce tamper-evident export bundles (Merkle-rooted, HSM-signed timestamp). 3) Include residency tags and retention policy metadata in exports. 4) Provide an API and S3-compatible export for evidence retrieval with stable identifiers and audit-trail links.
non_goals: We will not replace KMS/HSM vendor audit stores or change tenant key assignments. This work does not implement a full regulatory attestation UI or end-to-end legal certification process; it provides the cryptographic and data artifacts needed by compliance and legal teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reconciler ingests KMS CloudAudit and HSM SDK change logs from test regions and produces a single JSON export for a tenant with deterministic ordering. 2) Export includes residency and retention labels for each event. 3) Export is anchored with a Merkle root and an HSM-signed timestamp (or simulated HSM signature in staging). 4) API returns export bundles and metadata within SLA (95th percentile < 2s for metadata, export generation batching within acceptable window documented). 5) End-to-end test shows tamper detection: single-bit modification invalidates signature/merkle proof.
technical_design: Ingest layer: connectors for CloudAudit (GCP/AWS), HSM SDK event streams, and rotation pipeline webhooks. Normalizer: canonical event schema (timestamp, key_id, key_family, actor_id, event_type, region, residency_tag, retention_tag, rotation_version, source_id). Reconciliation algorithm: windowed ingest with deterministic ordering by (logical_timestamp, source_priority, source_sequence_id), conflict resolution policy documented. Export assembly: per-tenant Merkle tree built over canonical event records using SHA-256, export JSON schema with event list, merkle_root, hsm_timestamps, provenance indexes, and a human-readable summary. Anchoring: call HSM signing service to produce tamper-evident timestamp signature; fall back to KMS-signed timestamp for tenants without HSM. Storage: signed bundle stored in a compliance S3 bucket with object metadata for retention; index written to compliance-postgres for fast lookup. API: GET /v1/compliance/exports?tenant_id=&since= returns metadata; GET /v1/compliance/exports/{export_id} returns signed bundle.
data_handling_and_residency: Events must be kept and processed in a way that respects tenant residency settings. Ingest connectors will route raw events into region-specific processing lanes; reconciliation will only join events that the tenant's residency policy allows. Exports will explicitly tag the region of origin for each event and include a residency assertion block. For tenants with strict country residency, any cross-region event must be flagged and routed to a manual review queue.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (staging): wire up connectors for two non-production regions using simulated HSM signatures and run side-by-side with existing manual exports. Phase 2 (canary): enable for a small set of internal tenants and one low-risk customer; validate end-to-end proofs. Phase 3 (rollout): enable for all tenants with KMS-only proofs; customers with HSM integrations can opt in to HSM-signed exports. Provide backfill tool to generate reconciled exports for last 12 months where logs available. Backfill will be rate-limited and instrumented.
rollout_plan: - Week 1: Deploy ingest connectors to staging, run reconciliation in dry-run mode. - Week 2: Validate merkle roots and signature verification tests; security review. - Week 3: Canary with internal tenants; gather feedback. - Week 4: Open opt-in for HSM-signed exports for pilot customers. - Week 6: Default enable KMS-signed exports for all tenants and document retrieval API.
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalizer and reconcilers, property tests for ordering and idempotency, integration tests using recorded CloudAudit and HSM traces. End-to-end test: modify exported bundle and verify verification fails. Performance tests: measure reconciliation throughput and export generation latency across synthetic workloads approximating peak rotation bursts. QA steps: validate residency tagging, ensure per-tenant isolation, verify retention metadata maps to storage lifecycle policies.
operational_runbook: Runbook entries: how to re-run a reconciliation for a tenant, how to regenerate exports, how to verify HSM signatures, how to handle missing source logs, and escalation path for mismatched timestamps. Include commands for diagnostic endpoints: /debug/reconcile/{tenant}, /debug/verify-export/{export_id}. Monitor metrics: reconciler-lag, export-generation-duration, signature-failure-rate, exports-per-tenant.
security_considerations: HSM signing keys must remain in HSM and signing calls must be limited to minimal payload (merkle_root + metadata). All intermediate artifacts stored in compliance S3 must be encrypted at rest with tenant-specific KEKs where required. Access to export retrieval API must be audited and require tailored RBAC. Security review scheduled; expected items: HSM rate-limiting, mitigation for replay attacks, and proof-of-origin verification.
open_questions: 1) For tenants without HSM, do we accept KMS-signed timestamps as equivalent for compliance?
2) Should we store full raw logs alongside the signed bundle or only canonicalized events?
3) How long should we retain exports vs. source logs for regulatory requests?
4) What SLA do legal/compliance teams expect for on-demand export generation vs. pre-generated exports?
5) Is a Merkle root anchored to an external ledger (e.g., public anchor) required by auditors?
notes_and_progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after Compliance spike; initial design drafted and shared with infra and security.
2026-03-11: Architecture sync with HSM vendor (Thales). Vendor confirmed they can sign 500 ops/sec but require batching; we will group merkle roots into 1s bins.
2026-03-11: Decided to use SHA-256 Merkle tree and include canonical JSON serialization to ensure deterministic roots.
2026-03-12: Security requested proof-of-concept for signature verification and replay protection; Marcus started a POC branch (see PR below).
2026-03-12: Blocker noted: HSM SDK 4.x has breaking change for signature format; need to align with ops to upgrade HSM nodes in staging before canary.
2026-03-12: Added residency policy check to reconciliation to prevent cross-region joins for tenants with strict residency.

qa_checklist: Verify deterministic ordering with fuzzed timestamps and sequence collisions.
Run signature verification test that flips a byte and expects failure.
Confirm residency flags are present on each event in the exported bundle.
Test backfill tool on a 3-month window without exceeding source API rate limits.
Validate API pagination and metadata correctness for large tenant exports.
final_notes: This ticket centralizes cross-region key events into a single, auditable artifact. Focus on deterministic canonicalization, HSM anchoring where available, and strict residency enforcement. Next immediate actions: finish POC PR verification, coordinate HSM SDK upgrade schedule with ops, and schedule security review by 2026-03-15.
